description: Classification of one collected event, schema version 1 (CLAUDE.md section 8). Answer only from the given text. Use null when the text does not say.

product.description: Name of the product or company the event is about, as the text names it.

category.description: What kind of product it is, in a few words, for example 'remote desktop' or 'PDF editor'.

event_type.description: price: a price increase or a new paywall. forced_account: the product now requires a login or a cloud account. license: a license change that restricts use. shutdown: a product or feature is discontinued. acquisition: the company is acquired. api_lockdown: an API is closed, priced or rate-limited. listing: a business is for sale. pain: repeated complaints with no single event.

value_per_user.description: How much one user pays or would pay.

incumbent_moat.description: What keeps users with the current product. network: other users are there. data: a data set others do not have. seo: search rankings. code: the software itself, or its UX. none: nothing keeps them.

heavy_lifting_available.description: True when the text names open-source software that does the hard part of the product.

heavy_lifting_names.description: Names of that open-source software, for example 'ffmpeg'. Empty when the text names none.

local_rules.description: National rules the product must follow, such as tax or law. none: no local rules apply. AT: Austria. DE: Germany. DACH: Germany, Austria and Switzerland. other: another country.

evidence_of_paying.description: Verbatim quotes from the text that show people pay or would pay. Each under 30 words. Empty when there are none.

quote.description: One verbatim quote from the text that best shows the pain. Under 30 words.

confidence.description: How sure you are of this classification, from 0.0 to 1.0.
